name: execute_code
description:
Run an agent-supplied Python script inside a sandboxed Docker container. The script can read input pods (mounted as files at /workspace/inputs/), produce output files (anything written to /workspace/outputs/ auto-mints as pods returned in the result), and optionally seal stdout into a new pod with declared privacy class. Network access is denied by default — pass `egress_allowlist` to allow specific domains.

Use for: data analysis (pandas/matplotlib), image manipulation (PIL/opencv), PDF processing (pymupdf), document generation (reportlab/openpyxl), OCR (pytesseract), audio/video transcoding (ffmpeg), running test scripts, ad-hoc Python that needs libraries beyond what Emi's other tools expose.

Do NOT use for: simple HTTP calls (use http_request), reading filesystem on the host (use bash_manager), browser automation (use playwright_manager), one-line text manipulation (just do it in your reasoning step).

inputs.name: source
inputs.description: Python script body. Runs as a standalone file; you do not need `if __name__ == "__main__":`. Input pods live at /workspace/inputs/, write output files to /workspace/outputs/.

inputs.name: input_pod_ids
inputs.description: Pod URIs to make available as files in /workspace/inputs/. Pods are resolved at courier scope before the container starts.

inputs.name: fs_allowlist
inputs.description: Extra host paths to mount read-only inside the sandbox at /workspace/host_<basename>. Use sparingly; prefer input_pod_ids.

inputs.name: egress_allowlist
inputs.description: Domains the script is allowed to reach (e.g. ['api.openai.com', 'fal.run']). Default empty = no network. Advisory in v1: network IS opened when this is non-empty, and all egress is logged; per-domain enforcement is v1.1.

inputs.name: timeout_s
inputs.description: Per-call execution timeout in seconds. Default 30. Hard cap 300 (5 minutes); beyond that, factor into a routine.

inputs.name: response_pod_kind
inputs.description: If set, stdout is sealed into a new pod with this privacy class (e.g. 'health.private', 'financial.private'). The tool returns response_pod_id instead of inline stdout.

inputs.name: requirements
inputs.description: Extra pip packages to install before running. SLOW (15-60s per package). Only use if a needed library isn't in the base image (which already includes pandas, numpy, pillow, opencv, pymupdf, requests, etc.).

outputs.description: Human-readable summary: exit code, duration, byte counts, pod ids if any.
Structured payload: ok, exit_code, duration_ms, stdout (or null if sealed), stderr, stdout_truncated, response_pod_id, output_pod_ids, egress_logged.

arguments_prompt:
Arguments for execute_code:
source: str                                # the Python script
language: str = 'python'                   # python only in v1
input_pod_ids: list[str] = []              # mounted at /workspace/inputs/
fs_allowlist: list[str] = []               # extra host paths (read-only mount)
egress_allowlist: list[str] = []           # domains allowed (default deny)
timeout_s: float = 30.0                    # hard cap 300
response_pod_kind: Optional[str] = None    # seal stdout in pod with this class
requirements: list[str] = []               # extra pip installs (slow)

metadata.planner_description: Run a Python script in a Docker sandbox with pre-installed data/image/PDF/web libraries. Pod-aware input/output. Network denied by default. Use for analysis, transcoding, document work, anything needing pandas/PIL/pymupdf/etc.
